title: fix: keep large workspace recovery packs off the Gateway thread
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Reconciling a large managed workspace serializes its entire rollback pack on the Gateway thread before sending it to SQLite. A single operation can contain more than 120 MB of old file contents, delaying connected clients.

## User Impact

Large workspace reconciliations stop copying rollback packs through Gateway-thread serialization. Recovery, conflict handling, atomic acceptance, and journal correlation retain their existing behavior. No configuration, database schema, projection, or stored-format changes are required.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Git worker prepares a publication copy, and the SQLite broker transfers its ArrayBuffer outside the serialized command envelope. The original pack remains available for rollback and lost-reply recovery. Oversized-mutation diagnostic parsing and hashing run in the SQLite worker.

The journal is already cleared atomically when the accepted baseline is published. It contains one operation's rollback snapshot, not accumulated history: one synthetic reconciliation of 15,813 files produces a 120.8 MB pack. Dropping those old bytes before acceptance would break rollback, so no compaction or persistence change is justified.

Production growth is 93 lines for explicit transferable ownership through the existing worker transport and worker-side diagnostics; tests have no net growth. The replaced main-thread diagnostic implementation is removed. No cache or new owner is introduced. Lease and quiescence code is unchanged. Main's later #200643 changes the outer lease wrapper, preserves its callback contract, and does not overlap this mutation transport change.

## Evidence

The mutation target passes on head `872e422382dfc123aceadbe53b139021fd5e6b77`: every candidate's maximum active segment is below 50 ms and below both A/A controls. All twelve runs pass content/freshness checks. Exact-head [CI 44114615303](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44114615303) and [security/dependency/CI gates](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/44119217771) pass. [ClawSweeper's final-head source review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/200623#issuecomment-6951451433) has zero findings; completed performance evidence is now published below.

### Workload and acceptance

Two identical baseline controls, then five alternating baseline/candidate pairs in fresh processes on the same synthetic btrfs fixture. Require candidate mutation synchronous segments below 50 ms, lower main CPU than both controls, and fewer serialization copies without a total-cost regression. Baseline production source is `ae0d37b3c442c1ff4c06ea9a30e85a7dd4514093`; both arms use identical committed benchmark scripts from the final head. The fixture has 62,000 files, a 35.18 GiB synthetic agent database with 10,000 sessions, and 15,813 incompressible changed files. Every measured pack is exactly 120,778,221 bytes. Host load is recorded in each report.

Run from each frozen source arm with Node 26.12.1 and Git 2.47.3:

```sh
node --expose-gc --import ./scripts/tsx.mjs scripts/perf/local-workspace-checkpoint-measure.ts \
  --output /mnt/lane/fixture --mode reconcile --requests 1 --burst 1 \
  --files 62000 --file-bytes 19050 --reconcile-changed-files 15813 \
  --reconcile-random-bytes 7600 --instrument timing --mutation-segments \
  --reuse-fixture --agent-db-fixture /seed-agent.sqlite --report result.json
```

The owner-boundary workload uses real reconciliation, Git, files, SQLite and worker threads through the existing synthetic container-execution seam. It is not live Gateway/model or actual guest-pause evidence, and it does not reproduce the reported production 1.1-second stall. No production data or service changes were used.

### Completed A/A and five-pair comparison

Values are median / nearest-rank p95 across five samples; at n=5, p95 is the maximum. MB is decimal.

| Metric | Baseline A | Candidate B |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mutation maximum active segment | 60.91 / 64.89 ms | 7.93 / 10.40 ms |
| Mutation main CPU | 360.61 / 474.13 ms | 50.38 / 64.55 ms |
| Mutation main V8 allocations | 18.64 / 19.83 MB | 1.53 / 1.89 MB |
| Main serialization output | 247.053 / 247.053 MB | 5.490 / 5.490 MB |
| SQLite-bound transferred buffers | 121.902 / 121.902 MB | 121.894 / 121.894 MB |
| SQLite-bound cloned buffers | 0 | 0 |
| Mutation elapsed | 1,145.04 / 1,482.27 ms | 579.68 / 874.72 ms |
| Reconciliation owner elapsed | 46.24 / 48.34 s | 42.69 / 46.04 s |
| Whole-operation main CPU | 2.33 / 2.98 s | 1.96 / 2.49 s |
| Whole-operation Node process CPU | 34.99 / 36.22 s | 31.92 / 35.20 s |
| Whole-operation main V8 allocations | 267.99 / 273.96 MB | 254.08 / 263.18 MB |
| End RSS | 1,504.08 / 1,658.86 MB | 1,261.24 / 1,371.68 MB |
| Mutation raw timer gap | 61.06 / 65.32 ms | 13.97 / 74.58 ms |
| Whole-operation raw event-loop delay | 70.39 / 77.66 ms | 71.70 / 111.35 ms |

A/A controls: maximum active segments 67.93 and 65.37 ms; mutation CPU 423.07 and 412.08 ms; serialization 247.053 MB each. Candidate maximum active segments: 7.93, 7.26, 10.40, 8.26, 7.16 ms. Median mutation CPU falls 86.0%, serialization output 97.8%, and V8 allocation 91.8%. Reconciliation elapsed and total Node CPU improve 7.7% and 8.8% respectively.

The baseline already transferred its serialized envelope: avoided copies are before transfer. The candidate adds one 120.8 MB publication copy in the Git worker, retains the original for rollback, and removes about 241.6 MB of Gateway serialization output plus uncounted compression/framing copies. Git-to-main transfers carry the additional publication buffer without cloning it. SQLite-bound wire volume is effectively unchanged. V8 allocation excludes external ArrayBuffer storage; Node process CPU includes workers but excludes Git subprocesses.

### Timing qualification and retained outliers

The probe reports active event-loop time between 1 ms timer ticks as a conservative synchronous-segment bound, including nested callbacks, Promise microtask drains and synchronous waits. Controlled 120 ms CPU/microtask and synchronous Atomics workloads both report at least 120 ms; an asynchronous 120 ms wait reports under 1 ms active time. CPU/allocation/elapsed exclude the final 2 ms sampling drain. Byte counts observe the actual broker sends without decoding payloads.

Raw delay tails did not uniformly improve: the final candidate has a 74.58 ms mutation timer gap and a 111.35 ms whole-operation delay. These are retained, and no claim is made that all timer delays or live Gateway latency are below 50 ms. During the 74.58 ms mutation gap, the active segment remained 7.26 ms. The 111.35 ms whole-operation maximum is outside the measured oversized mutation.

An earlier complete raw-timer campaign had candidate gaps 7.08, 8.14, 6.97, 8.04 and 63.51 ms; its outlier was retained and landing held. Follow-up profiling reproduced a 73.84 ms gap with only 0.057 ms main CPU, matching a 73.95 ms CPU-profile interval entirely marked idle. That justified separating active work from event-provider/host idle delay, followed by the complete new A/A and five-pair campaign above. The earlier unprofiled 63.51 ms sample remains individually unclassified. Preliminary callback-only probes undercounted microtask drains and are excluded. This proof establishes mutation work reduction, not a general scheduling-latency improvement.

### Correctness and checks

145 focused tests passed, with two existing skips: local-workspace store/diagnostics/projection, reconciliation main-thread/recovery, and SQLite input. The extended lost-reply regression fails on the exact parent because the publication buffer remains attached; it passes with the fix while preserving original rollback bytes and durable recovery receipts. Diagnostics are observed from the actual worker. No affected Control UI imports were found. Codex autoreview of the production change and final benchmark correction found no actionable P0–P2 findings.

`pnpm check:changed` ran against the starting parent. Type and boundary checks passed. Patch lint/line-cap findings were repaired; targeted lint, core/script types, formatting and diff checks pass. Five dead exports reproduce on that exact parent and candidate: two from #200538 (`resolveMcpOAuthLinkRedirectUrl`, `resolveBrowserAuthOrigin`), one from #200545 (`markRunningToolCalls`), one from #199838 (`validateArtifactMetadata`), and one from #200019 (`qualificationAdmissionContract`). These are main regressions requiring follow-up, not passing checks. Current PR CI is green; no inherited-CI merge exception is needed.

An earlier CI failure rejected a benchmark prototype override's lint suppression. The benchmark now uses its existing loader hooks without that override or suppression. The exact failed suite passes all 14 tests, and final CI is green. Runtime code has been unchanged throughout the benchmark corrections.
